Manchester United head coach Michael Carrick has insisted that he is not expecting to be dismissed within the next 24 hours following the club’s disappointing 3-0 home defeat to Bournemouth. The result has intensified pressure on Carrick, with United continuing to struggle for consistent performances and positive results this season. As reported by Fabrizio Romano on X on Sunday, speaking after the defeat, Carrick acknowledged the uncertainty surrounding his position but maintained that he was not anticipating any immediate decision regarding his future. “I totally understand the situation. I’m not expecting anything in particular, to be honest. I’m carrying on as normal and, you know, I love this place,” he said. The United manager also reiterated his commitment to the club, stressing that he would always act in what he believes to be Manchester United’s best interests. Manchester United suffer eighth winless match against Bournemouth EPL: Bournemouth thrash Man United 3-0, pressure mounts on Carrick EPL: Carrick to bench Brruno for Bournemouth clash — Report Carrick’s comments come at a difficult time for the club, as the latest setback raises further questions about the team’s form and the direction of the season. Despite the growing scrutiny, the head coach appears determined to continue with his responsibilities while awaiting developments from the club’s hierarchy. For now, Carrick has made it clear that he is not expecting an imminent dismissal, although uncertainty remains over what the coming days could bring for Manchester United and their manager.
